mainTopic: Sending only one שעיר המשתלח and which one (ראשון or אחרון), then the new פרק's משנה on the two שעירי יום הכפורים
overview: This amud finishes the discussion of the שעיר המשתלח. Someone challenges the rule that only one is sent, since sometimes several goats are burned. The answer is that the פסוק says "אותו" about the scapegoat, which limits it to one. Then two reports in the name of רבא disagree about which goat is sent when several are available. רב שימי says the last one, because the כפרה is completed with it. רב פפי says the first one, following רבי יוסי's rule of מצוה בראשון. The גמרא first tries to find this rule in רבי יוסי's ruling about the three labeled קופות, but rejects that source. It settles on his ruling about a lost-and-found קרבן פסח instead. After the הדרן, a new פרק opens with a משנה about the two שעירי יום הכפורים. The משנה covers how the goats should ideally match, and what to do if one dies before or after the lottery. It ends with the מחלוקת between the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה about the leftover goat.

steps.title: Challenge: We burn several goats, so why not send several?
steps.stepSummary: A challenger compares sending the scapegoat to burning goats. Sometimes several goats are burned even though the Torah speaks of one, so maybe several scapegoats can be sent too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does he burn his whole flock?
steps.whatsHappening: Someone is challenging the idea that only one שעיר המשתלח may be sent. He points out that we sometimes burn several goats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah describes burning one goat, yet the משנה shows that sometimes several are burned. If one can become several there, the challenger asks why one cannot become several by the scapegoat.

keyTerms.meaning: his flock (here, sarcastically: a whole group of goats)
burns
and is it so that...? (a sharp rhetorical challenge)

phrases.english: And does he burn his flock?
phrases.notes: This is a rhetorical question: sometimes more than one goat does get burned, so why should only one be sent?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion earlier about limiting the scapegoat to one animal.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only one שעיר המשתלח may be sent
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Burning goats can involve several animals even though the Torah speaks of one, so sending should be able to involve several as well.

steps.title: Answer: The verse says "it" only about the scapegoat
steps.stepSummary: The burning and the sending are not comparable. By the scapegoat the Torah writes "אותו" ("it"), which limits it to one. By the burning it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it comparable? There, about burning, "it" is not written. Here, about the scapegoat, "it" is written.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is answered: the two cases are different because of one word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "אותו" works as a limiting word, meaning only this one animal. Burning has no such word, so several goats can be burned. Sending is limited to one.

keyTerms.meaning: is it comparable? (rejects a comparison)
there
here
"it" (a limiting word meaning this one alone)

steps.whatToRemember: Only one שעיר המשתלח is ever sent, because the Torah says "אותו".

phrases.english: Is it comparable?
There (about burning), "it" is not written,
here (about the scapegoat), "it" is written.
phrases.notes: The word "it" means just one animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי דָּמֵי הָתָם לָא כְּתִיב אוֹתוֹ הָכָא כְּתִיב אוֹתוֹ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases based on wording in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Burning and sending work the same way, so several animals could be sent.
steps.terutzMaskana: "אותו" by the scapegoat limits it to one animal; burning has no such limit.

steps.title: A dispute: send the first goat or the last one?
steps.stepSummary: Two students report different rulings in the name of רבא. רב פפי says the first scapegoat is sent. רב שימי says the last one is sent.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב פפי said in the name of רבא, he sends the first one. רב שימי said in the name of רבא, he sends the last one.
steps.whatsHappening: Since only one scapegoat can be sent, the גמרא now brings a מחלוקת about which one it is when several are available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the situation where extra pairs of goats were brought, so there is more than one possible scapegoat. Both opinions are quoted from רבא, so the dispute is really about what רבא held.

keyTerms.meaning: in the name of
the first
the last
he sends (the scapegoat away)

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּמַר, רַב פַּפִּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא אָמַר:
phrases.english: It was stated: Rav Pappi said in the name of Rava:
He sends the first one,
and Rav Shimi said in the name of Rava:
He sends the last one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר רַב פַּפִּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 2: once we know only one is sent, the question becomes which one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two reports of רבא: the first scapegoat is sent (רב פפי), or the last one is sent (רב שימי).

steps.title: The last-goat view makes sense, but why the first?
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי's view is easy to understand, because the כפרה is completed with the last goat. The גמרא asks what reasoning lies behind רב פפי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is understandable according to רב שימי (בר אשי) in the name of רבא, who said the last one is sent. He holds that since the כפרה was completed with it, it is used. But רב פפי in the name of רבא, what does he hold?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains one side of the מחלוקת and then asks for the reason behind the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last goat is the one with which the כפרה was finished, so sending it is logical. The first goat seems to have no such advantage, so the גמרא asks why רב פפי would choose it.

keyTerms.meaning: it is understandable (according to one side)
but (introduces the side that is hard to explain)
he holds
since the atonement was completed with it

steps.confusionAlert: "בשלמא... אלא..." here is not an attack that disproves רב פפי. It is a genuine request for his reasoning.

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא רַב שִׁימִי (בַּר אָשֵׁי) מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא,
phrases.english: Granted, Rav Shimi (bar Ashi) in the name of Rava,
who said he sends the last one —
he holds: since the atonement was completed with it.
phrases.notes: The last goat finishes the כפרה, so it is the one sent.

phrases.english: But Rav Pappi in the name of Rava,
what does he hold?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the reasoning behind the two opinions of step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the reasoning behind רב פפי's view that the first scapegoat is sent?

steps.title: The first-goat view follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי follows רבי יוסי, who holds that when there are several items for a מצוה, the first one is used (מצוה בראשון).
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי יוסי, who said: the מצוה is with the first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: רב פפי relies on a general principle of רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The principle מצוה בראשון says the first item gets priority for a מצוה. So the first scapegoat, not the last, should be sent.

keyTerms.meaning: he holds like
the מצוה is done with the first one

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties a specific יום הכפורים question to a general principle that applies to מצוות across ש״ס.

phrases.english: He holds like Rabbi Yosei,
who said: the מצוה is with the first.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי דְּאָמַר מִצְוָה בָּרִאשׁוֹן
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב פפי follows רבי יוסי's principle of מצוה בראשון.

steps.title: Which ruling of רבי יוסי? A first candidate: the three containers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי יוסי says מצוה בראשון. It suggests his ruling about the three containers used for collecting the Temple funds, which were marked א, ב, ג.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which רבי יוסי? If you say the רבי יוסי of the containers, as we learned: רבי יוסי says, there were three containers of three סאין each, with which they collect the donation from the chamber, and א, ב, ג was written on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is looking for the source of רבי יוסי's principle. It starts by quoting a משנה about three marked containers, setting up the next step that explains the markings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The money in the Temple chamber was taken out in three containers, each holding three סאין. Each container was labeled א, ב, or ג. On its own, the משנה does not yet say why they were labeled. The ברייתא in the next step explains that.

keyTerms.meaning: which?
if you say (often a suggestion that will be rejected)
containers, baskets
סאה measures (a unit of volume)
they take out the donation (תרומה) from the Temple chamber

steps.confusionAlert: "אילימא" usually signals a first suggestion that the גמרא may reject later. Don't assume this is the final answer.

phrases.english: Which Rabbi Yosei?
phrases.notes: Which statement of רבי יוסי teaches this principle?

phrases.english: If you say the Rabbi Yosei of the containers,
as we learned in a mishna (Rabbi Yosei says):

phrases.aramaic: שָׁלֹשׁ קוּפּוֹת שֶׁל שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁלֹשׁ סְאִין
phrases.english: three containers of three se'a each
with which they collect the donation from the chamber,
and alef, beit, gimmel was written on them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אִילֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי דְּקוּפּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the source of the principle cited in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which teaching of רבי יוסי establishes מצוה בראשון?

steps.title: רבי יוסי explains the labels: the first container is used first
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי explaining the א, ב, ג labels. They show which container was filled first, so that its money can be used first, because מצוה בראשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught: רבי יוסי said, why was א, ב, ג written on them? To know which of them was filled first, so as to bring from it first, because the מצוה is with the first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that the labels exist to support the principle of מצוה בראשון. This completes the suggested source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The labels let the Temple treasurers know which container was filled first, so they spend its money first. This explicitly states מצוה בראשון, which seems to be the source for רב פפי's view about sending the first goat.

keyTerms.meaning: in order to know
was filled from the chamber (the תרומה was taken)
from it

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי labels the containers so the first one can be used first, because מצוה בראשון. This is only a proposed source for רב פפי's ruling. The next step rejects it.

phrases.english: And it was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yosei said:
Why was alef, beit, gimmel written on them?
To know which of them was filled first,
so as to bring the money from it first,
because the מצוה is with the first.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לָמָּה כָּתוּב עֲלֵיהֶן אב״ג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the candidate source from step 6 by explaining the purpose of the labels.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי holds מצוה בראשון, the principle behind רב פפי's view
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יוסי explains the א, ב, ג labels on the containers of תרומת הלשכה

steps.title: The containers proof does not work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from the א, ב, ג containers. The first container may have been used first only because it was ready earlier, not because of a general rule of מצוה בראשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps at the time when the first container was fit to be used, the last one was not yet fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof it just brought from the three containers. It shows that the containers case does not really prove רבי יוסי holds מצוה בראשון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the containers, the first one was filled and ready before the later ones even existed. So using it first may just be because it was ready first. With the goats, both animals are available at the same moment, so the containers case is not a true parallel.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps / maybe. A word that often opens a rejection of a proof.
At the time when
Was fit / was usable
The first one
The last one

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying רבי יוסי rejects מצוה בראשון. It is only saying this particular source cannot prove it.

phrases.english: Perhaps at the time when the first one was fit,
phrases.notes: This refers to the first container of Temple funds.

phrases.english: the last one was not yet fit.
phrases.notes: The later containers had not yet been collected.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 7
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The containers case cannot serve as a source for רבי יוסי's general rule of מצוה בראשון.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the containers case, the items were not available at the same time. The first may have been used only because it was ready first. This is unlike the goats, which are available together.

steps.title: A better source: רבי יוסי on the lost פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי יוסי's ruling about a קרבן פסח that was lost and later found after a replacement was set aside. He says the first animal should be used, unless the second is of better quality.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the source is רבי יוסי's ruling about the פסח, as we learned: Someone set aside an animal for his פסח, and it was lost. He set aside another one in its place, and afterward the first one was found, so now both are standing before him. The חכמים say he may offer whichever one he wants. רבי יוסי says the מצוה is to use the first one, but if the second one is better quality, he should bring the second.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected the containers proof, the גמרא offers a replacement source for רבי יוסי's rule. This is the case of a lost and found קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here both animals are fully fit and available at the same moment, so the problem from Step 8 does not apply. Even so, רבי יוסי still prefers the first animal. That shows a real principle of מצוה בראשון, which supports רב פפי's view that the first scapegoat is sent.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Introduces a new approach after rejecting the old one.
One who sets aside / designates an animal for a קרבן
The קרבן פסח (Passover offering)
Choicer / of superior quality

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי's מצוה בראשון comes from the lost-and-found פסח. In that case, both animals are equally available, and he still prefers the first. The exception is when the second animal is better quality.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives רב פפי a solid foundation. He follows רבי יוסי's rule of מצוה בראשון, so the first scapegoat is sent. רב שימי's view rests on a different reason: the כפרה is completed with the last goat (step 4).

phrases.english: Rather, it is Rabbi Yosei regarding the Pesach offering (as we learned):
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets, דִּתְנַן ("as we learned"), and some have it.

phrases.english: One who set aside his Pesach animal, and it was lost,
and he set aside another in its place,
and afterward the first one was found,
and now both of them are standing before him —
phrases.notes: Both animals are fit at the same time. This is the key difference from the containers case.

phrases.english: he may offer whichever of them he wants,
these are the words of the Sages.
Rabbi Yosei says: the מצוה is with the first one,
and if the second was of better quality than it —
he should bring it (the second).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the source rejected in Step 8 with a stronger one
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי holds the general principle of מצוה בראשון, which is the basis for רב פפי's view (Step 5).
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי's dispute with the חכמים about a lost קרבן פסח that was found after a replacement was designated.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing פרק הוציאו לו
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula marks the end of פרק הוציאו לו.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק הוציאו לו.
steps.whatsHappening: This line simply marks that פרק הוציאו לו has ended. A new פרק is about to begin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional farewell said when finishing a פרק. It expresses the hope to return and learn it again. It does not add any new הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. The formula said when finishing a פרק.
They brought out to him. The name of the פרק just completed.

phrases.english: We will return to you, "Hotzi'u Lo"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final discussion in Step 9

steps.title: The two goats of יום הכפורים should ideally be identical
steps.stepSummary: The new פרק opens with a משנה. Ideally the two שעירי יום הכפורים should match in appearance, height, value, and time of purchase. However, they are valid even if they do not match, or if they were bought on different days.
steps.simpleTranslation: The two goats of יום הכפורים: their מצוה is that both should be equal in appearance, in height, and in value, and that they be bought together. But even if they are not equal, they are valid. If he bought one today and one tomorrow, they are valid.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה about the two goats of יום הכפורים. It sets out the ideal way to choose them, and then says what happens if that ideal is not met.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה separates the best way to do the מצוה from what is required after the fact. Matching the goats is the preferred way. But a mismatch in looks, height, value, or purchase date does not make them invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: The two goats of יום הכפורים: one offered to ה׳, one sent to עזאזל
Their מצוה, meaning the ideal way they should be done
Equal / identical
Their purchase / acquisition
Valid

steps.confusionAlert: "מצותן" here means the ideal way (לכתחילה), not a requirement. That is why the משנה goes on to say the goats are כשרין even when they are not equal.

phrases.english: The two goats of Yom Kippur —
their מצוה is that both of them should be equal
in appearance, in height, and in monetary value
and that they be acquired together.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין שָׁוִין — כְּשֵׁרִין.
phrases.english: And even if they are not equal — they are valid.

phrases.aramaic: לָקַח אֶחָד הַיּוֹם וְאֶחָד לְמָחָר — כְּשֵׁרִין.
phrases.english: If he acquired one today and one tomorrow — they are valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק after the הדרן in Step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ideally, the two goats should be identical in appearance, height, value, and time of purchase. However, they remain valid even if they differ, or were bought on different days.

steps.title: If one of the two goats dies
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if one goat dies before the lottery, a new partner is bought for the surviving goat. If it dies after the lottery, a whole new pair is brought and lots are drawn again.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one of them died: if it died before he drew the lots, he takes a partner for the second goat. If it died after he drew the lots, he brings another pair and draws lots on them from the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its laws about the two goats. It now deals with a problem case: one of the goats died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Timing is the key. Before the lottery, neither goat has a role yet, so the survivor just needs a new partner. After the lottery, each goat already has a fixed role, so a simple replacement is not enough. A brand-new pair must go through a fresh lottery.

keyTerms.meaning: He drew the lots (the גורל that decides which goat is for ה׳ and which is for עזאזל)
A partner or a pair
From the beginning, anew

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new source. It is the same משנה from step 11, still continuing.

phrases.english: If one of them died,
if it died before he drew the lots,
he takes a partner for the second goat.
phrases.notes: The survivor gets a matching partner, and then the lottery is done.

phrases.english: And if it died after he drew the lots,
he brings another pair
and draws lots on them from the beginning,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from step 11, moving from the ideal matching of the goats to the case where one of them dies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a goat dies before the lottery, a partner is bought for the survivor. If it dies after the lottery, a new pair is brought and a fresh lottery is held.

steps.title: The stipulation for the new pair
steps.stepSummary: After the new lottery, the כהן גדול declares that the new goat whose lot matches the dead goat's role will take its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he says: If the goat for ה׳ died, this goat that the lot for ה׳ fell on will stand in its place. And if the goat for עזאזל died, this goat that the lot for עזאזל fell on will stand in its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains how the new pair connects to the old one. The כהן גדול makes a formal declaration that the new goat with the matching role replaces the dead goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one goat from the new pair is actually needed, namely the one whose role matches the dead goat. The declaration sets which goat steps in. This means one goat will be left over, and the next step deals with it.

keyTerms.meaning: The goat for ה׳ (the one offered as a קרבן)
The goat sent away to the wilderness (the שעיר המשתלח)
Will stand in its place, will replace it

phrases.english: And he says:
If the goat for God died,

phrases.aramaic: זֶה שֶׁעָלָה עָלָיו הַגּוֹרָל לַשֵּׁם יִתְקַיֵּים תַּחְתָּיו,
phrases.english: this one on which the lot for God came up shall stand in its place,
and if the goat for Azazel died,

phrases.aramaic: זֶה שֶׁעָלָה עָלָיו הַגּוֹרָל לַעֲזָאזֵל יִתְקַיֵּים תַּחְתָּיו.
phrases.english: this one on which the lot for Azazel came up shall stand in its place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Details the procedure after the new lottery described in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The new goat whose lot matches the dead goat's role takes its place, through a spoken declaration.

steps.title: What happens to the extra goat
steps.stepSummary: The extra goat grazes until it gets a blemish. Then it is sold, and the money goes to buy a נדבה, because a חטאת צבור is not left to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the second goat grazes until it becomes blemished. Then it is sold, and its money goes to a voluntary offering, because a communal חטאת is not left to die.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now deals with the leftover goat that has no job. This is the view of the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a חטאת that is no longer needed can be left to die (a חטאת מתה). The תנא קמא says this rule does not apply to a חטאת צבור. So the extra goat is not destroyed. It waits for a blemish so it can be sold, and the money is used for נדבה.

keyTerms.meaning: It grazes until it becomes blemished (unfit for the מזבח)
A voluntary offering (here, public עולות bought with the money)
A communal sin-offering
Left to die (the rule for certain unused individual חטאות)

steps.confusionAlert: "השני" here means the extra goat that is not used. It does not simply mean "the second goat of the original pair." Exactly which goat this is gets discussed later in the גמרא.

phrases.english: And the second (extra) goat grazes until it becomes blemished,
and it is sold, and its money goes to a gift-offering,
because a communal sin-offering is not left to die.
phrases.notes: This is the reason for the ruling: the rule of leaving a חטאת to die applies only to an individual's חטאת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Handles the leftover goat created by the new pair in steps 12 and 13.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the principle אין חטאת צבור מתה, which רבי יהודה disputes in the next step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra goat grazes until blemished and is sold for נדבה, because a חטאת צבור is never left to die.

steps.title: רבי יהודה says the extra goat is left to die
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees with the תנא קמא and rules that the extra goat is left to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: It should be left to die.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה argues on the previous ruling about the extra goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא said a חטאת צבור is never left to die. רבי יהודה rules that this extra goat is left to die anyway, so the rule of a חטאת מתה applies here too. This creates a מחלוקת about the leftover goat.

keyTerms.meaning: It should be left to die

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: It should be left to die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא's ruling in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the extra goat is left to die.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the two goats depend on each other
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה adds that if the blood of the goat for ה׳ spills, the שעיר המשתלח must die, and if the שעיר המשתלח dies, the blood is poured out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה also said: If the blood spilled, the goat to be sent away must die. If the goat to be sent away died, the blood is poured out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a second ruling. In his view, the two goats are tied together, so a problem with one cancels the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the blood of the goat for ה׳ spills before it is sprinkled, a new pair is needed. רבי יהודה says the old שעיר המשתלח cannot stay. It must die, and both goats come from the new lottery. The same works in the other direction: if the שעיר המשתלח dies, the blood already collected is poured out and a fresh pair is used.

keyTerms.meaning: And he also said, introducing another ruling from the same person
The blood spilled (before it was sprinkled)
The goat that is sent away (to עזאזל)

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא: if a goat dies after the lottery, a new pair is brought, and the extra goat is sold for נדבה because אין חטאת צבור מתה. רבי יהודה: the extra goat is left to die, and the two goats are linked, so if one is lost, the other is lost too.

phrases.english: And furthermore Rabbi Yehuda said:
If the blood spilled,
the goat that is sent away must die.
If the goat that is sent away died,
the blood is poured out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ruling from רבי יהודה, following his opinion in step 15.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי יהודה sees the two goats as one linked unit, which the גמרא will analyze later.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, losing the blood of the goat for ה׳ means the שעיר המשתלח must die, and losing the שעיר המשתלח means the blood is poured out.
